correctness.rationale: The exact norm identity follows from positive finite-dimensional Volterra kernels, Minkowski/Tonelli and near-Dirac approximate identity. Dyadic/logarithmic partition yields upper/lower finite-N inequalities and a tail at most b^{-K}+exp(-b^{K+1}). The normalized error is at most 2K/N plus that tail for all r including 1 and infinity. Mass conservation verifies r=1; strong strictness for r>1, spectral-spacing limits via disjoint intervals and uniform shifted Riemann sums, including the infinity limit. This is an analytic proof, not an inference from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: Focus source arXiv:2608.20266v2 proves qualitative mixed-space obstruction with the same b=2 kernels, not an exact single-block finite-dimensional endpoint norm, log-periodic leading constant, explicit finite-N error, arbitrary b or spacing transition. Inspected older Blunck 2001 maximal regularity applies primarily to p>1 UMD settings. Focused public and mathematical-index searches and owned-ledger deduplication found no stronger statement. Residual risks are itemized, and no uniqueness beyond inspected literature is claimed.
residual_risks: An unindexed general theorem giving asymptotic norms of positive Banach-valued L1 convolutions could imply the present log-periodic coefficient.
The cited textbook example on diagonal semigroups was not inspected in full; its qualitative endpoint obstruction is not logically equivalent to the sharp formula.
Only finitely many primary sources and searchable public-index records were inspected; absence of a hit is not a novelty certificate.

value.rationale: The work computes the sharp growth coefficient of the canonical finite spectral cutoff underlying an endpoint maximal-regularity failure, in a natural full family of sequence exponents and spectral spacing ratios. It gives a deterministic finite-N error and describes dense-versus-sparse spectral phase limits, which are quantitative invariants not provided by the qualitative nonboundedness theorem. The exact coefficient is mathematically motivated by cutoff calibration, not an arbitrary slice.
